thesis: A P&C insurer is one of the few equities that is structurally long the exact macro fact dominating this tape: at a 5.24% 10Y, every dollar of float rolls into reinvestment yields far above the coupons maturing out of the portfolio, and that flows to net investment income quarter after quarter rather than as a one-off. key_risk: Catastrophe losses. Q3 is Atlantic hurricane season and a P&C underwriting quarter can be ruined by events that have nothing to do with the investment-income thesis; I could not fetch a Q3 catastrophe-loss estimate, so that leg of the print is genuinely unknown to me going in.
counter_argument: Positioning on the sell side is moving the wrong way: the analyst recommendation trend has deteriorated over four months, with bullish share down 7.6 points to 25.7% and outright sell ratings rising from 1 in June to 5 in September. Insiders have not bought a share on the open market in six months against 25 sales worth $36.3M. The strongest bear case is that the relative strength is late-cycle crowding into a defensive name and the analysts moving to sell are early - the 398 target is the prior range high, so the trade needs a breakout the sell side does not expect.

thesis: UPDATE TO AN EXISTING POSITION opened 2026-10-12 at 262.00; last 257.84, inside the accumulation zone and 30.6% below the 371.47 range high. The zone and target are unchanged. The update is informational and it cuts in the buyers favour: the reason the whole defense complex is down - no FY2027 appropriation, a CR to 12-11 locking spend at 2026 levels, and midterm risk to future budgets - is a *funding-timing* story, and nuclear submarine and carrier construction is the line item least exposed to it, being multi-year, already-appropriated, and sole-source. It is answered only partially, and the answer is the pacing rather than the thesis: this is an accumulation in thirds with no stop and a two-quarter build, so waiting for 11-03 is a reason to stage the entry, not to skip it. The honest version of the disagreement is that buying the first third here costs money if Harned is right about timing.

thesis: The street cannot model this company. Vicor has beaten consensus EPS in four consecutive quarters by 341.2%, 126.6%, 19.8% and 58.5% - not a streak of small beats but a persistent failure of the sell side to size a power-conversion business levered to datacenter power build-out, covered by only ten analysts. key_risk: Insiders have been distributing heavily - 567 sales worth $202.6M against zero open-market purchases over six months - which is a large number for a company this size and means the people closest to the business have been selling into exactly the run this trade is buying. Compounding it, ATR14 is 19.39, or 7.25% a day: two ordinary adverse sessions is a 15% drawdown, the 225.00 stop is 15.7% away by construction, and an earnings gap does not respect it. Sized at 1.5% for that reason.
counter_argument: The beat record is probably being competed away, and that is the strongest case against. Consensus for the September quarter has risen from 0.1428 a year ago to 1.03 - the bar is seven times higher than the one Vicor cleared by 341%, so the street has substantially caught up and the next surprise is far more likely to be ordinary. Pair that with the insider selling and the honest reading of the 26% drawdown is not a pullback in an uptrend but informed money leaving ahead of the first print the company has to clear a realistic estimate on.

thesis: The street cannot model this company. Vicor has beaten consensus EPS in four consecutive quarters by 341.2%, 126.6%, 19.8% and 58.5% - not a streak of small beats but a persistent failure of the sell side to size a power-conversion business levered to datacenter power build-out, covered by only ten analysts. The stock has just given back 26% from its 2026-10-01 high of 331 into a 244.53 low on 10-13 and closed that session at 267.24, near the top of its own range, which is where a high-beta name that is still 55% above its 120-day low tends to resume rather than roll over.
key_risk: Insiders have been distributing heavily - 567 sales worth $202.6M against zero open-market purchases over six months - which is a large number for a company this size and means the people closest to the business have been selling into exactly the run this trade is buying. Compounding it, ATR14 is 19.39, or 7.25% a day: two ordinary adverse sessions is a 15% drawdown, the 225.00 stop is 15.7% away by construction, and an earnings gap does not respect it. Sized at 1.5% for that reason.
counter_argument: The beat record is probably being competed away, and that is the strongest case against. Consensus for the September quarter has risen from 0.1428 a year ago to 1.03 - the bar is seven times higher than the one Vicor cleared by 341%, so the street has substantially caught up and the next surprise is far more likely to be ordinary. Pair that with the insider selling and the honest reading of the 26% drawdown is not a pullback in an uptrend but informed money leaving ahead of the first print the company has to clear a realistic estimate on.
